title: Ways to create objects in Java
answer: The normal way is `new`, which allocates an object and invokes a constructor. Objects can also be obtained through factories that internally create objects, reflection via a `Constructor` object, cloning for classes that support `Cloneable`, and deserialization for serializable classes. Reflection still invokes a constructor; cloning and Java deserialization can create object state without executing the class's ordinary constructor in the same way as `new`. In production code, prefer explicit constructors or factories unless a framework or specialized mechanism genuinely requires the alternatives.
